claim: Neurosphere formation is commonly used as a surrogate for neural stem cell (NSC) function.
source: Neurosphere formation is commonly used as a surrogate for neural stem cell (NSC) function but the relationship between neurosphere-initiating cells (NICs) and NSCs remains unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about common practice in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript and general scientific knowledge.

claim: The relationship between neurosphere-initiating cells (NICs) and NSCs remains unclear.
source: Neurosphere formation is commonly used as a surrogate for neural stem cell (NSC) function but the relationship between neurosphere-initiating cells (NICs) and NSCs remains unclear.
evidence: This statement reflects the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: Adult mouse lateral ventricle subventricular zone (SVZ) NICs can be prospectively identified and isolated by flow cytometry as Glast mid EGFR high PlexinB2 high CD24 −/low O4/PSA-NCAM −/low Ter119/CD45 − (GEPCOT) cells.
source: We prospectively identified, and isolated by flow cytometry, adult mouse lateral ventricle subventricular zone (SVZ) NICs as Glast mid EGFR high PlexinB2 high CD24 −/low O4/PSA-NCAM −/low Ter119/CD45 − (GEPCOT) cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by the flow cytometry data and functional assays presented in Figure 1.

claim: GEPCOT cells were highly mitotic in vivo based on BrdU incorporation.
source: They were highly mitotic and short-lived in vivo based on fate-mapping with Ascl1 and CreERT2 Dlx1.
evidence: This is supported by BrdU pulse experiments shown in Figure 1D demonstrating that 89 ± 4% of GEPCOTs were BrdU+ after a 24-hr pulse.

claim: GEPCOT cells were short-lived in vivo based on fate-mapping with Ascl1CreERT2 and Dlx1CreERT2.
source: They were highly mitotic and short-lived in vivo based on fate-mapping with Ascl1 and CreERT2 Dlx1.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping experiments in Figure 2B-C showing rapid decline in labeled cells over time.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells were quiescent in vivo.
source: In contrast, pre-GEPCOT cells were quiescent, expressed higher Glast, and lower EGFR and PlexinB2.
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data in Figure 4C showing only 3 ± 3% of pre-GEPCOT cells incorporated BrdU in 24 hours.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed higher Glast than GEPCOT cells.
source: In contrast, pre-GEPCOT cells were quiescent, expressed higher Glast, and lower EGFR and PlexinB2.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C-D showing GlasthighEGFR−/low profile for pre-GEPCOT cells.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed lower EGFR than GEPCOT cells.
source: In contrast, pre-GEPCOT cells were quiescent, expressed higher Glast, and lower EGFR and PlexinB2.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C-D showing EGFR−/low expression in pre-GEPCOT cells.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed lower PlexinB2 than GEPCOT cells.
source: In contrast, pre-GEPCOT cells were quiescent, expressed higher Glast, and lower EGFR and PlexinB2.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3C-D showing PlexinB2mid expression in pre-GEPCOT cells.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by neurosphere formation assays in Figure 4B showing only 1/1663 pre-GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed the stem cell marker Slc1a3-CreERT.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping data in Figure 4G showing 31–36% of pre-GEPCOT cells were labeled by Slc1a3-CreERT.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed the stem cell marker GFAP-CreERT2.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping data in Figure 3A and Figure 4I showing GFAP-CreERT2 labeled 29 ± 7% of pre-GEPCOT cells at 2 days after tamoxifen.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed the stem cell marker Sox2CreERT2.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping data in Figure 4H showing 87–93% of pre-GEPCOT cells were labeled by Sox2CreERT2.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells expressed the stem cell marker Gli1CreERT2.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping data in Figure 4F showing 7–13% of pre-GEPCOT cells were labeled by Gli1CreERT2.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells were long-lived in vivo.
source: Pre-GEPCOT cells could not form neurospheres but expressed the stem cell markers CreERT2 Slc1a3-CreER , T GFAP-CreER , T2 Sox2 , and CreERT2 Gli1 and were long-lived in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by fate-mapping data in Figures 3A and 4F-H showing sustained labeling of pre-GEPCOT cells for 60 days after tamoxifen treatment.

claim: GEPCOT NICs were ablated by temozolomide treatment.
source: While GEPCOT NICs were ablated by temozolomide, pre-GEPCOT cells survived and repopulated the SVZ.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5E showing only 10% of GEPCOTs remained 3 days after TMZ treatment.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells survived temozolomide treatment.
source: While GEPCOT NICs were ablated by temozolomide, pre-GEPCOT cells survived and repopulated the SVZ.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5F showing no significant change in pre-GEPCOT cell numbers after TMZ treatment.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells repopulated the SVZ after temozolomide treatment.
source: While GEPCOT NICs were ablated by temozolomide, pre-GEPCOT cells survived and repopulated the SVZ.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5O-P showing increased numbers of labeled GEPCOT cells arising from Slc1a3-CreERT and GFAP-CreERT2 labeled pre-GEPCOT cells after TMZ treatment.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bmi-1 depleted pre-GEPCOT cells.
source: Conditional deletion of the CreERT2 Bmi-1 polycomb protein depleted pre-GEPCOT and GEPCOT cells, though pre-GEPCOT cells were more dependent upon Bmi-1 for Cdkn2a ( p16 ) repression.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 6L and 7P showing reduced frequencies of pre-GEPCOT cells in Bmi-1 conditional knockout mice.

claim: Conditional deletion of Bmi-1 depleted GEPCOT cells.
source: Conditional deletion of the CreERT2 Bmi-1 polycomb protein depleted pre-GEPCOT and GEPCOT cells, though pre-GEPCOT cells were more dependent upon Bmi-1 for Cdkn2a ( p16 ) repression.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 6M and 7Q showing reduced frequencies of GEPCOT cells in Bmi-1 conditional knockout mice.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells were more dependent upon Bmi-1 for Cdkn2a (p16Ink4a) repression than GEPCOT cells.
source: Conditional deletion of the CreERT2 Bmi-1 polycomb protein depleted pre-GEPCOT and GEPCOT cells, though pre-GEPCOT cells were more dependent upon Bmi-1 for Cdkn2a ( p16 ) repression.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figures 6O and 7R showing Cdkn2a (p16Ink4a) expression was detected in pre-GEPCOT cells but rarely in GEPCOT cells from Bmi-1 deficient mice.

claim: Neural stem cells (NSCs) reside in two regions of the adult mammalian forebrain: the subgranular zone in the dentate gyrus and the subventricular zone in the lateral wall of the lateral ventricle (SVZ).
source: Neural stem cells (NSCs) reside in two regions of the adult mammalian forebrain: the subgranular zone in the dentate gyrus and the subventricular zone in the lateral wall of the lateral ventricle (SVZ).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work in the field.

claim: SVZ NSCs persist throughout adult life.
source: SVZ NSCs persist throughout adult life (Maslov et al., 2004; Molofsky et al., 2006; Imayoshi et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs give rise primarily to neurons in the olfactory bulb.
source: giving rise primarily to neurons in the olfactory bulb as well as some astrocytes in the olfactory bulb (Lois and Alvarez-Buylla, 1994; Lois et al., 1996; Doetsch et al., 1999b; Ahn and Joyner, 2005; Kuo et al., 2006; Lagace et al., 2007; Merkle et al., 2007; Imayoshi et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs give rise to some astrocytes in the olfactory bulb.
source: giving rise primarily to neurons in the olfactory bulb as well as some astrocytes in the olfactory bulb (Lois and Alvarez-Buylla, 1994; Lois et al., 1996; Doetsch et al., 1999b; Ahn and Joyner, 2005; Kuo et al., 2006; Lagace et al., 2007; Merkle et al., 2007; Imayoshi et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs give rise to oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum and cortex.
source: and oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum and cortex (Nait-Oumesmar et al., 1999; Menn et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs are quiescent in vivo.
source: In vivo, these NSCs are quiescent (Doetsch et al., 1999a; Pastrana et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs are resistant to anti-mitotic agents.
source: resistant to anti-mitotic agents (Morshead et al., 1994; Doetsch et al., 1999b, 2002; Giachino and Taylor, 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs are long-lived.
source: long-lived (Ahn and Joyner, 2005; Imayoshi et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SVZ NSCs are capable of regenerating the SVZ after injury.
source: and capable of regenerating the SVZ after injury (Doetsch et al., 1999b, 2002; López-Juárez et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: On average, 1.8 ± 0.4% of SVZ cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter).
source: On average, 1.8 ± 0.4% of SVZ cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter) and 75% of those neurospheres underwent multilineage differentiation (1.4 ± 0.3% of SVZ cells).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from neurosphere formation assays.

claim: 75% of neurospheres formed by SVZ cells underwent multilineage differentiation.
source: On average, 1.8 ± 0.4% of SVZ cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter) and 75% of those neurospheres underwent multilineage differentiation (1.4 ± 0.3% of SVZ cells).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from differentiation assays.

claim: 383 antibodies against 330 distinct cell surface antigens were systematically screened.
source: We systematically screened 383 antibodies against 330 distinct cell surface antigens
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: GEPCOT cells represent 3.2 ± 0.7% of young adult mouse SVZ cells.
source: GEPCOTs accounted for 3.2 ± 0.7% of all SVZ cells (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: On average, 36 ± 6% of GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter).
source: On average, 36 ± 6% of GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter) and 74% of those neurospheres underwent multilineage differentiation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on neurosphere formation assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 74% of neurospheres formed by GEPCOT cells underwent multilineage differentiation.
source: On average, 36 ± 6% of GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (>50 µm diameter) and 74% of those neurospheres underwent multilineage differentiation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on differentiation assays shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nearly all of the neurospheres formed by GEPCOT cells (91%) could be passaged.
source: Nearly all of the neurospheres (91%) could be passaged (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on passaging experiments.

claim: Each neurosphere formed by GEPCOT cells gave rise to 53 ± 41 multipotent secondary neurospheres upon dissociation and replating.
source: On average, each neurosphere gave rise to 53 ± 41 multipotent secondary neurospheres upon dissociation and replating, demonstrating self-renewal potential.
evidence: This is based on secondary neurosphere formation assays.

claim: After a 2 hour pulse of BrdU, 35 ± 2% of GEPCOTs were BrdU+ as compared to only 11 ± 4% of unfractionated SVZ cells.
source: After just a 2 hour pulse of BrdU, 35 ± 2% of GEPCOTs were already BrdU+ as compared to only 11 ± 4% of unfractionated SVZ cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on BrdU incorporation experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: After a 24-hr pulse of BrdU, 89 ± 4% of GEPCOTs were BrdU+ as compared to 47 ± 9% of unfractionated SVZ cells.
source: After a 24-hr pulse of BrdU, 89 ± 4% of GEPCOTs were BrdU+ as compared to 47 ± 9% of unfractionated SVZ cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on BrdU incorporation experiments shown in Figure 1D.

claim: GEPCOTs are highly mitotically active and enriched for dividing cells relative to unfractionated SVZ cells.
source: GEPCOTs are thus highly mitotically active and enriched for dividing cells relative to unfractionated SVZ cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the BrdU incorporation data showing high labeling of GEPCOTs.

claim: Nearly all GEPCOTs incorporated BrdU within 24 hr, indicating that few, if any, GEPCOTs are quiescent.
source: The observation that nearly all GEPCOTs incorporated BrdU within 24 hr indicates that few, if any, GEPCOTs are quiescent and that NICs are highly proliferative in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the BrdU incorporation data.

claim: NICs are highly proliferative in vivo.
source: The observation that nearly all GEPCOTs incorporated BrdU within 24 hr indicates that few, if any, GEPCOTs are quiescent and that NICs are highly proliferative in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the BrdU incorporation data showing that GEPCOTs, which are enriched for NICs, are highly proliferative.

claim: 2 days after tamoxifen treatment, Dlx1CreERT2 labeled 51 ± 6% of SVZ cells, 15 ± 6% of GEPCOTs, and 11 ± 4% of neurospheres.
source: 2 days after tamoxifen treatment, Dlx1CreERT2 labeled 51 ± 6% of SVZ cells, 15 ± 6% of GEPCOTs, and 11 ± 4% of neurospheres (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 7 days after tamoxifen, Dlx1CreERT2 labeling significantly declined to 8 ± 5% of SVZ cells, 0.7 ± 0.9% of GEPCOTs, and 0.9 ± 1% of neurospheres.
source: 7 days after tamoxifen this significantly (p<0.001) declined to 8 ± 5% of SVZ cells, 0.7 ± 0.9% of GEPCOTs, and 0.9 ± 1% of neurospheres (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 28 days after tamoxifen, only rare SVZ cells, GEPCOTs, and neurospheres were labeled by Dlx1CreERT2.
source: 28 days after tamoxifen only rare SVZ cells, GEPCOTs, and neurospheres were labeled (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Dlx1CreERT2-expressing NICs persist in vivo for less than 7 days.
source: Dlx1CreERT2-expressing NICs thus persist in vivo for less than 7 days.
evidence: This is inferred from the rapid decline in labeled cells shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 2 days after tamoxifen, Ascl1CreERT2 labeled 34 ± 7% of SVZ cells, 63 ± 8% of GEPCOTs, and 64 ± 6% of neurospheres.
source: 2 days after tamoxifen, Ascl1CreERT2 labeled 34 ± 7% of SVZ cells, 63 ± 8% of GEPCOTs, and 64 ± 6% of neurospheres (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 7 days after tamoxifen, the fraction of GEPCOTs and neurospheres labeled by Ascl1CreERT2 significantly declined to 40 ± 4% and 45 ± 3%, respectively.
source: 7 days after tamoxifen a similar fraction of SVZ cells remained tdTomato+ (35 ± 3%) but the fraction of labeled GEPCOTs and neurospheres significantly (p<0.01) declined to 40 ± 4% and 45 ± 3%, respectively (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 28 days after tamoxifen, only 16 ± 0.9% of SVZ cells, 16 ± 0.6% of GEPCOTs, and 19 ± 1.0% of neurospheres were labeled by Ascl1CreERT2.
source: 28 days after tamoxifen only 16 ± 0.9% of SVZ cells, 16 ± 0.6% of GEPCOTs, and 19 ± 1.0% of neurospheres were labeled.
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 60 days after tamoxifen, labeling by Ascl1CreERT2 further decreased to 7.5 ± 1.2% of SVZ cells, 12 ± 0.8% of GEPCOTs, and 8 ± 3% of neurospheres.
source: This further decreased to 7.5 ± 1.2% of SVZ cells, 12 ± 0.8% of GEPCOTs, and 8 ± 3% of neurospheres at 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Most Ascl1CreERT2-expressing NICs persist in vivo for less than 28 days.
source: This demonstrates that most Ascl1CreERT2-expressing NICs persist in vivo for less than 28 days.
evidence: This is inferred from the decline in labeled cells over time shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cells labeled with Gli1CreERT2, Slc1a3-CreERT, or Sox2CreERT2 exhibited a sustained contribution to the pools of SVZ cells, GEPCOTs, and NICs for at least 60 days after tamoxifen administration.
source: In contrast to cells labeled with Dlx1CreERT2 or Ascl1CreERT2, cells labeled with Gli1CreERT2, Slc1a3-CreERT, or Sox2CreERT2 exhibited a sustained contribution to the pools of SVZ cells, GEPCOTs, and NICs for at least 60 days after tamoxifen administration (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figures 2D-F.

claim: There is a long-lived NSC population in the SVZ that replenishes NICs and is marked by Gli1CreERT2, Slc1a3-CreERT, and Sox2CreERT2 expression.
source: This suggested the existence of a long-lived NSC population in the SVZ that replenishes NICs and is marked by Gli1CreERT2, Slc1a3-CreERT, and Sox2CreERT2 expression (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is inferred from the sustained labeling patterns observed in fate-mapping experiments.

claim: Without tamoxifen, virtually no SVZ cells expressed the tdTomato reporter in GFAP-CreERT2; Rosa26-loxp-tdTomato mice.
source: Without tamoxifen, virtually no SVZ cells expressed the reporter.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 2 days after tamoxifen, the tdTomato+ cells labeled by GFAP-CreERT2 were GlasthighEgfr−/lowPlexinB2midCD24−/lowO4/PSA-NCAM−/lowTer119/Cd45− (pre-GEPCOT) cells.
source: 2 days after tamoxifen, the tdTomato+ cells labeled by recombination by the GFAP-CreER stem cell marker were GlastT2highEgfr−/lowPlexinB2midCD24−/lowO4/PSA-NCAM−/lowTer119/Cd45− (CD24 expression is not shown here), which we describe as 'pre-GEPCOT' cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3C.

claim: By 28 days after tamoxifen, GlastmidEgfrhighPlexinB2highCD24−/lowO4/PSA-NCAM−/lowTer119/CD45− GEPCOT cells were also labeled by GFAP-CreERT2.
source: By 28 days after tamoxifen, GlastmidEgfrhighPlexinB2highCD24−/lowO4/PSA-NCAM−/lowTer119/CD45− GEPCOT cells were also labeled.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells comprise 6 ± 3% of SVZ cells.
source: The gating strategy to identify the GFAP-expressing pre-GEPCOT population that comprises 6 ± 3% of SVZ cells.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 3E.

claim: 21 ± 7% of pre-GEPCOT cells were GFAP+.
source: GFAP expression was heterogeneous within the pre-GEPCOT population, with 21 ± 7% being GFAP
evidence: This is based on antibody staining experiments.

claim: Only very rare pre-GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (1/1663 cells).
source: In contrast, only very rare pre-GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (1/1663 cells) and only 0.3 ± 0.4% (9/1973 cells) formed adherent colonies (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on neurosphere formation assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Only 0.3 ± 0.4% (9/1973 cells) of pre-GEPCOT cells formed adherent colonies.
source: In contrast, only very rare pre-GEPCOT cells formed neurospheres (1/1663 cells) and only 0.3 ± 0.4% (9/1973 cells) formed adherent colonies (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on adherent colony formation assays shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Only 3 ± 3% of pre-GEPCOT cells incorporated BrdU after a 24-hr pulse.
source: Although 47 ± 9% of SVZ cells and 89 ± 4% of GEPCOT cells (Figure 1D) incorporated a 24-hr pulse of BrdU in these experiments, only 3 ± 3% of pre-GEPCOT cells incorporated BrdU in the same mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on BrdU incorporation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Only 4 ± 2% of pre-GEPCOT cells incorporated BrdU after a 2-week pulse.
source: Similarly, 60 ± 6% of SVZ cells and 91 ± 3% of GEPCOT cells (Figure 1D) incorporated a 2-week pulse of BrdU in these experiments, but only 4 ± 2% of pre-GEPCOT cells incorporated BrdU (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on BrdU incorporation experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Pre-GEPCOT cells are quiescent in the SVZ.
source: These data indicate that pre-GEPCOT cells are quiescent in the SVZ.
evidence: This is inferred from the low BrdU incorporation data.

claim: Dlx1CreERT2 did not label any pre-GEPCOT cells at 2, 7, or 28 days after tamoxifen treatment.
source: Dlx1CreERT2, which labeled 51 ± 6% of all SVZ cells and 15 ± 6% of GEPCOTs at 2 days after tamoxifen treatment (Figure 2B), did not label any pre-GEPCOT cells at 2, 7, or 28 days after tamoxifen treatment (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Ascl1CreERT2 labeled fewer than 1% of pre-GEPCOT cells at 2, 7, 28, and 60 days after tamoxifen.
source: Ascl1CreERT2, which labeled 34 ± 7% of all SVZ cells and 63 ± 8% of GEPCOTs at 2 days after tamoxifen (Figure 2C), labeled fewer than 1% of pre-GEPCOT cells at 2, 7, 28, and 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Neither Dlx1CreERT2-expressing GEPCOT NICs nor Ascl1CreERT2-expressing GEPCOT NICs gave rise to significant numbers of pre-GEPCOT qNSCs in vivo under steady-state conditions.
source: Neither the Dlx1CreERT2-expressing GEPCOT NICs nor the Ascl1CreERT2-expressing GEPCOT NICs gave rise to significant numbers of pre-GEPCOT qNSCs in vivo, at least under steady-state conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of labeling of pre-GEPCOT cells by these Cre lines.

claim: Gli1CreERT2 sustainably labeled 7–13% of pre-GEPCOT cells at 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen treatment.
source: Gli1CreERT2, which sustainably labeled 8–19% of all SVZ cells and 26–40% of GEPCOTs for 60 days after tamoxifen treatment (Figure 2D), also sustainably labeled 7–13% of pre-GEPCOT cells at 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen treatment (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Slc1a3-CreERT labeled 31–36% of pre-GEPCOT cells 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen.
source: Slc1a3-CreERT, which sustainably labeled 21–48% of all SVZ cells and 61–72% of GEPCOTs for 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 2E), also labeled 31–36% of pre-GEPCOT cells 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Sox2CreERT2 sustainably labeled 87–93% of pre-GEPCOT cells 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen.
source: Sox2CreERT2, which sustainably labeled 49–65% of all SVZ cells and 92–97% of GEPCOTs for 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 2F), also sustainably labeled 87–93% of pre-GEPCOT cells 2 to 60 days after tamoxifen (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4H.

claim: All CreERT2 alleles that labeled pre-GEPCOT cells exhibited sustained labeling of pre-GEPCOT cells, GEPCOTs, NICs, and unfractionated SVZ cells.
source: Moreover, every CreERT2 allele that labeled pre-GEPCOT cells exhibited sustained labeling of not only pre-GEPCOT cells but also GEPCOTs, NICs, and unfractionated SVZ cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the fate-mapping data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: 2 days after tamoxifen administration to GFAP-CreERT2; Rosa26-loxp-tdTomato mice, 29 ± 7% of pre-GEPCOT cells were tdTomato+.
source: 2 days after tamoxifen administration to GFAP-CreERT2; Rosa26-loxp-tdTomato mice, the tdTomato label was present mainly in pre-GEPCOT cells. On average, 29 ± 7% of pre-GEPCOT cells were tdTomato+ whereas only 6.7 ± 1.9% of GEPCOT cells, 2.2 ± 0.5% of PSA-NCAMhighCD24mid neuroblasts (Pastrana et al., 2009), and 3.0 ± 0.8% of other SVZ cells were labeled (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 2 days after tamoxifen, only 6.7 ± 1.9% of GEPCOT cells were labeled by GFAP-CreERT2.
source: On average, 29 ± 7% of pre-GEPCOT cells were tdTomato+ whereas only 6.7 ± 1.9% of GEPCOT cells, 2.2 ± 0.5% of PSA-NCAMhighCD24mid neuroblasts (Pastrana et al., 2009), and 3.0 ± 0.8% of other SVZ cells were labeled (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: GFAP-CreERT2 recombines efficiently in pre-GEPCOTs but not GEPCOT NICs in vivo.
source: These data indicate that GFAP-CreERT2 recombines efficiently in pre-GEPCOTs but not GEPCOT NICs in vivo.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential labeling patterns shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 28 days after tamoxifen treatment, the percentage of labeled pre-GEPCOT cells increased to 44 ± 5.8%.
source: 28 days after tamoxifen treatment, the percentage of labeled pre-GEPCOT cells increased to 44 ± 5.8% of cells (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: 28 days after tamoxifen, the percentages of labeled GEPCOTs, neuroblasts, and other SVZ cells significantly increased to 32 ± 4.7%, 35 ± 6.8%, and 20 ± 2.2%, respectively.
source: The percentages of labeled GEPCOTs, neuroblasts, and other SVZ cells also increased significantly (p<0.01) by 28 days–32 ± 4.7%, 35 ± 6.8%, and 20 ± 2.2%, respectively.
evidence: This is based on fate-mapping experiments shown in Figure 4I.

claim: GFAP-CreERT2-expressing pre-GEPCOT cells include qNSCs that give rise to NICs, neuroblasts, and other SVZ cells.
source: These data suggest GFAP-CreERT2-expressing pre-GEPCOT cells include qNSCs that give rise to NICs, neuroblasts, and other SVZ cells (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is inferred from the fate-mapping data showing increasing labeling of downstream populations over time.

claim: GFAPhigh cells were observed at the center of pinwheel structures with a single primary cilium on the apical surface contacting the ventricle and a long basal process.
source: Consistent with prior results (Mirzadeh et al., 2008), we observed GFAPhigh cells at the center of the pinwheel structures with a single primary cilium on the apical surface contacting the ventricle and a long basal process (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount immunostaining shown in Figure 4L and is consistent with prior studies.

claim: Many pre-GEPCOT cells have the morphology and position of type B1 cells in the SVZ.
source: Since many pre-GEPCOTs recombined with GFAP-CreERT2 but virtually no GEPCOTs did (Figure 4I), these data indicate that many pre-GEPCOT cells have the morphology and position of type B1 cells in the SVZ.
evidence: This is inferred from the GFAP expression, morphology, and position of pre-GEPCOT cells.

claim: EGFRhigh cells had type C cell morphology: round, unciliated, and generally not contacting the ventricle.
source: In contrast, EGFRhigh cells had type C cell morphology: round, unciliated, and generally not contacting the ventricle, consistent with Doetsch et al. (2002) (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount immunostaining shown in Figure 4M and is consistent with prior studies.

claim: Many GEPCOT cells have the morphology and position of type C cells.
